statement: This map is an index into the repository, not an authority over it. Future Gate audits must verify each relevant entry against the current source before relying on it -- a stale entry is a documentation bug, not a contract change. @2 (post-M42 Governance Baseline Reconciliation) replaces the long per-entry engineering-history notes @1 accumulated with a short contractSummary; full Work-Unit-by-Work-Unit history for a domain lives in that milestone's own closure report under docs/archive/milestones/, not here. lastVerifiedCommit records the commit at which this entry's primary/supporting paths were last confirmed to exist and its contractSummary confirmed accurate -- it is not a claim that every historical behavioral detail was re-derived.

canonicalState.contractSummary: Defines StateModelSchema/StateModel, the canonical overall on-disk state shape and its schema version. New canonical sections are added as optional, additive fields (see e.g. M42's `defects`).

candidateStateValidation.contractSummary: readStateModel() runs assertCompatibleVersion before StateModelSchema.safeParse; writeStateModel() also gates the candidate model version before persistence. Project/store behavior mirrors this in src/state/project-store.ts.

atomicStateWrite.contractSummary: atomicWriteFileSync() is the sole atomic-write primitive; writeStateModel() and safe-writer helpers build on it.

runlogStore.contractSummary: appendRunlogEvent/readRunlogEventIds/inspectRunlogHealth plus all build*Event() builder functions (~45+, including M42's buildDefectCandidateDiscoveredEvent/buildDefectStatusChangedEvent). RunlogEvent.type is a free string field -- new event types never require a schema change.

canonicalJson.contractSummary: canonicalizeJsonValue/canonicalJsonStringify/computeCanonicalPayloadDigest -- the single canonicalization implementation, introduced in M23 and reused directly by M28 and M42 (defect fingerprinting).

sha256Digest.contractSummary: sha256Hex() is the sole hashing primitive; computeCanonicalPayloadDigest builds on it.

exitCodeOwner.contractSummary: ExitCode const map and ExitCodeValue type; AiqtError carries an ExitCode, register-commands.ts maps thrown errors to the process exit code.

boundedInput.contractSummary: readBoundedTextFile() plus readStdinText() are the size-bounded input readers used by every file/stdin import command.

jsonOutput.contractSummary: renderJson() plus the CommandResult shape; register-commands.ts is the central --json dispatch point. See commandResultContract below and docs/governance/cli-machine-contract.md for the full external contract.

previewBehavior.contractSummary: Canonical --preview implementation (M9/M20). A repeated per-command pattern (see graph repair's --dry-run/--apply and M42's `aiqt defects` --preview flags), not a single shared preview module.

evidenceSchema.contractSummary: EvidenceRecordSchema and ArtifactReference/ArtifactKind (M22); the sole evidence-taxonomy owner, reused directly by M28's evidenceSelector.artifactKinds and referenced by M42's DefectEvidenceRef.

evidenceTrust.contractSummary: TRUST_LEVEL_ORDER and meetsTrustLevel(), co-located with the evidence schema (M22): unverified < self_reported < repository_local < platform_verified.

checkpoint.contractSummary: CheckpointSchema/CheckpointIssueSchema/ValidationResultSchema/AcceptanceCriterionResultSchema. M42's discovery engine reads validationCommands/issues directly, adding no second checkpoint owner.

packetLifecycle.contractSummary: Creation via buildPacketContext/computePacketAuditMetadata (invoked from next.command.ts); cancellation via next-cancel.command.ts orchestrating buildPacketCancelledEvent and applyWorkUnitCancelTransition.

executionSessions.contractSummary: Execution session schema and protocol constants (M26); service functions getExecutionSessions/findSessionsForWorkUnit/findAnySessionForPacket (M27).

externalExecutionAdapters.contractSummary: Normalizes Claude Code adapter results into the generic execution-result shape (M27); generic external-adapter CLI path lives in execution-external-request.command.ts.

evidenceGatePolicy.contractSummary: Policy/rule schema and bounds (MAX_POLICIES, MAX_RULES_PER_POLICY, etc.), introduced in M28.

evidenceGateSimulation.contractSummary: evaluateRule()/aggregateOverallResult()/simulate() -- the sole pure, read-only simulation entry point, introduced in M28. Never imports runlog-store, atomic-write, or workflow-state-store.

statusCommand.contractSummary: runStatus(); as of M28 optionally includes a read-only evidenceGate summary field.

workflowAssessment.contractSummary: M32 established assessWorkflow() and WORKFLOW_RECOMMENDATION_RULES as the authoritative workflow-position, recommendation, integrity, and project-status owner. Legacy helpers remain only as compatibility adapters over assessWorkflow().

reviewCommand.contractSummary: runReviewCommand() and the runReview()/review-rules evaluation it delegates to.

versioningPolicy.contractSummary: package.json's version field is the single canonical version source, independent of AIQT_SCHEMA_VERSION, milestone tags, and release tags/Releases. runVersionCheck()/version-check-cli.ts implement the automated checks (pnpm version:check); relevant-paths.ts is the sole change-relevance allowlist.

pullRequestGovernance.contractSummary: The PR template (risk-band header, conditional sections, no N/A placeholders) plus versioning.md's 'Pull Request merge gate' section are the authoritative PR contract: CI green, mergeable, no blocking review issue, human maintainer review. `pnpm pr:ready` (pr-ready-cli.ts) is the required local pre-PR check before `gh pr create` -- it reuses runVersionCheck() so it can never drift from CI's own version-check job. Merging is a manual human action (a merge commit, never squash/rebase) -- there is no automated merge workflow and no machine-readable approval label; an earlier `approved-for-merge` label + auto-merge-on-label GitHub Actions workflow was deliberately removed in favor of this simpler, fully manual model. Direct-push-to-main comparison uses resolveDirectPushBase (push-base.ts) via GitHub's github.event.before, not an assumed HEAD~1.

ciWorkflows.contractSummary: The sole GitHub Actions workflow (name: Validate), on every push to main and every pull request. One Node 24 job named `validate` (no Node 22/24 matrix -- Node 22 was retired from CI after the M21-M34 era) running checkout(fetch-depth 0) -> pnpm/node setup with pnpm store cache -> install -> typecheck -> lint -> build -> test -> version:check (local, then the blocking PR-base or direct-push-to-main comparison). IH-02 replaced M35-WU04's 6-job/3-shard fan-out with this single job because GitHub bills per job rounded up to the whole minute: measured 18 billed runner-minutes for 6 jobs vs 14 for one, plus 5 redundant setup cycles and a dist/ artifact round-trip removed. A `concurrency` group cancels superseded pull_request runs only; push-to-main runs are the authoritative post-merge gate and are never cancelled.

testRuntimePolicy.contractSummary: pool:'threads', no global testTimeout/concurrency override. tests/workload-timeout-policy.ts is the single shared source for the two class-scoped timeout constants (SPAWNING_SUITE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=15000, HEAVY_SPAWNING_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=25000). package.json's validate script runs build before test so tests/integration/built-binary-smoke.test.ts has a real dist/index.js. Full M34 history: docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m34-*.md. See testInventoryPolicy for the workload-classification layer built on top of this.

autonomousRunContract.contractSummary: M36's bounded, policy-checked autonomous-execution mechanics: lifecycle status enum + transition table, candidate/safety-assessment/budget/execution-policy/result-state/evidence-packet schemas, a real (structured-args, shell:false, policy-checked) command-execution surface, and the evidence-binding pipeline that decides resultState/recommendedHumanAction. No CLI command invokes live execution against a real coding model from this repository; no merge; no deployment. Full engineering history: docs/archive/milestones/m36/m36-autonomous-run-contract.md.

testInventoryPolicy.contractSummary: test-inventory-cli.ts is the single, reusable static classifier for every tests/**/*.test.ts file -- workload class, feature domain, criticality, subprocess/filesystem/Git/built-binary usage, and inline-timeout presence. The deletion-evidence contract for any future test removal or merge lives in docs/governance/test-rationalization-policy.md. Inventory/classification only -- does not own vitest.config.ts or any test's timeout/concurrency behavior (see testRuntimePolicy).

commandResultContract.contractSummary: M33's authoritative CommandResult/Issue/AiqtError/ExitCode shape. renderJson()/renderHuman() are the sole shared renderers; familyFailureResult()/missingProjectResult()/parserErrorToResult() are the shared failure-result builders every command family (including M40 release, M41 validation, M42 defects) uses. External-facing contract documented at docs/governance/cli-machine-contract.md. Full engineering history: docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m33-wu01-command-result-contract.md.

historicalCompatibilityFixtures.contractSummary: cli.test.ts's 'aiqt CLI entrypoint' describe block carries the original per-milestone command-set/exit-code assertions; later milestones (M22+) split their own dedicated historical-compatibility test files rather than extending it.

sandboxBackendContract.contractSummary: M38's real, opt-in, Linux-only (OCI-container) sandboxed execution backend: DockerSandboxBackend, real capability evaluation with no 'proceed unsandboxed' branch, `aiqt autonomous agent-import --live` gated at two independent config layers, crash-recovery via autonomous-cleanup.command.ts. Network-enabled live execution is permanently unsupported (plain Docker has no destination-allowlist). Escape-testing coverage (tests/integration/sandbox-escape-testing.test.ts) confirms parent-repo/host-home/sibling-worktree/secret/network isolation. Full engineering history and threat model: docs/archive/milestones/m38/m38-sandbox-threat-model.md and m38-sandbox-platform-decision.md.

executionGuidance.contractSummary: M39's shared, provider-neutral ExecutionGuidance decision owner: composeExecutionGuidance() (classification, context manifest, continuation capsule, validation guidance) is the sole entry point `aiqt next`/`aiqt next --preview` call via next-selection-helpers.ts's buildExecutionGuidanceForWorkUnit, guaranteeing preview/apply parity by construction. M41 extended buildValidationGuidance with testImpactInput (see adaptiveTestSelection) -- purely additive, can only add a requiredNow step. Full engineering history: docs/archive/milestones/m39/AIQT_Milestone_39_Build_Specification.md.

releaseGovernance.contractSummary: M40's release-readiness/status/prepare/validate/notes surface: aggregates CI/version/risk/provenance state into one read-only readiness view and a governed release-decision record, without itself creating a tag, GitHub Release, or performing a merge. Full engineering history: docs/archive/milestones/m40/build-spec.md and closure-report.md.

releaseRiskAssessment.contractSummary: computeReleaseRiskStatus()/computeReleaseApprovalAuthority() implement the exact repository four-band scale (0-24 green/25-49 yellow/50-74 orange/75-100 red; agent-approvable below 50) for RELEASE risk specifically -- a distinct domain from M42's remediation-risk.ts (remediation implementation risk) and from defect severity/confidence. Both reuse the same numeric boundaries, not the same scoring inputs or the same function.

releaseProvenance.contractSummary: Builds the provenance record (WU commits/tags, milestone tag, baseline/final commit, validation evidence) a GitHub Release's required sections are drafted from; does not itself publish a Release.

historicalReleaseReconstruction.contractSummary: M44's transient historical-reconstruction contract: HistoricalReleaseTarget/ReconstructionAssessment are never a ReleaseCandidate/ReleaseDecision (releaseGovernance/releaseProvenance own those). Reuses ReleaseEvidenceStatus (verified/reconstructed/partial/missing/waived) from release-governance.schema.ts unchanged; adds HistoricalEvidenceConflict as a blocking-finding-style disagreement between two evidence items rather than a sixth evidence-item status. historical-evidence.ts is the pure Git/file evidence-collection layer (discoverSemverReleaseTags, selectBaseRelease's ancestry-only fail-closed algorithm, discoverMilestoneReferences); reconstruction-engine.ts is the pure reconstruction-quality decision (computeReconstructionStatus -- never produces `existing_release` itself) and M40 mapping (mapToReleaseIntentRequest -> the exact releaseGovernanceService.ReleaseIntentRequest shape, never a parallel candidate model) plus retrospective-notes banner reusing renderReleaseNotesMarkdown verbatim; historical-reconstruction-service.ts is the sole orchestration point (mirrors release-governance-service.ts's split) that sequences evidence collection, calls the engine, calls the existing assessReleaseDecision, and (WU44-04) layers verifyExistingGithubRelease on top -- reusing services/github-release-client.ts's existing getReleaseByTag (releaseProvenance's supporting owner, M40-WU04's single bounded GitHub adapter) verbatim, never a new HTTP client, never createReleaseDraft. `unverified` (no token / non-owner-repo identity / API failure) is always distinct from an authoritative `not_found`; a found published release upgrades the outcome to `existing_release`, never fabricated locally. M40 remains the sole readiness/risk/approval-authority owner, including its forward-looking 'tag already exists' readiness check, which correctly fires for every historical reconstruction since the tag is real. `aiqt release history`/`release reconstruct <tag> [--token-env]` are both read-only. Full engineering history: docs/milestones/active/m44/build-spec.md (docs/milestones/completed/m44/ at closure).

adaptiveTestSelection.contractSummary: M41's sole deterministic test-selection algorithm: selectTestImpact() (pure selection) plus selectTestImpactWithFeedback() (the feedback-aware wrapper every consumer calls). Explicit validationCommands are always mandatory; a broad-blast-radius path hit always escalates to full_required; unresolved trusted prior failures downgrade to broaden_required. Selection decides what runs now -- it is never deletion evidence (see docs/governance/test-rationalization-policy.md Sec 6a). TEST_IMPACT_SELECTION_VERSION='test-impact@1' is carried on every selection. Full engineering history: docs/archive/milestones/m41/build-spec.md and closure-report.md.

validationSelectExplain.contractSummary: aiqt validation select/explain -- read-only, never mutates workflow state, reuses buildExecutionGuidanceForWorkUnit directly (byte-for-byte parity with `next --preview`'s own testImpact field verified by test). No second selection path exists.

defectContract.contractSummary: M42's DefectRecord/DefectStatus/DefectSeverity/DefectConfidence/DefectTriageDecision/RemediationDecision contract, persisted as StateModel's optional, additive `defects` section (introduced at AIQT_SCHEMA_VERSION 0.6.0; current schema 0.7.0 as of M45). The remediation queue is this list filtered to QUEUE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES, not a second stored list or a `.aiqt/defects.*` file. DEFECT_TRANSITIONS is the sole lifecycle transition table; illegal transitions fail closed. computeDefectFingerprint dedups on structural identity only, never free text.

defectRemediationQueue.contractSummary: aiqt defects discover|list|inspect|triage|queue|transition|remediate|record-validation. Discovery (failed_validation/checkpoint_issue/human_reported only; other sources explicitly reported unsupported) never authorizes remediation. Triage (computeTriageDecision) is pure/deterministic; remediation risk (remediation-risk.ts) is scored from scope alone, independent of defect severity, using the same four-band scale as releaseRiskAssessment but a distinct scoring input -- risk >=50 requires explicit human approval or nothing is persisted. Validation evidence, not agent assertion, controls resolution/reopen. No live execution surface is invoked; this is the bounded external-agent handoff/request path, not a second execution engine. M45's scheduled defect_remediation task kind calls prepareRemediation directly (same function `aiqt defects remediate` calls) -- it does not bridge to M36-M39 live sandboxed execution (sandbox-run-execution-service.ts remains reachable only from autonomous-agent-import.command.ts); see maintenanceScheduling for the explicit reasoning. Full engineering history: docs/archive/milestones/m42/build-spec.md and closure-report.md.

maintenanceScheduling.contractSummary: M45's persistent maintenance-schedule/occurrence contract, persisted as StateModel's optional, additive `maintenanceSchedules`/`maintenanceActiveOccurrence` sections (AIQT_SCHEMA_VERSION 0.6.0 -> 0.7.0). A schedule is timing intent, never execution/approval authority: MaintenanceSchedulePolicy.maxAutomaticRisk is schema-bounded to <=49, so it can only lower remediation-risk.ts's existing <50 automatic-approval ceiling, never raise it. maintenanceActiveOccurrence is a nullable singleton (never an array), making 'no parallel scheduled maintenance' structural rather than a runtime check. No `.aiqt/schedules.*` file or second database exists. maintenance-due-engine.ts is the pure, injectable-clock due-selection/occurrence-identity engine (selectDueSchedule, computeNextDueAtAfterEvaluation -- anchor-aligned, always strictly after the evaluation time, so a host offline for N periods never replays a backlog); maintenance-schedule-service.ts is the pure CRUD layer `aiqt maintenance schedule add|list|inspect|update|enable|disable|remove` orchestrate (none of those commands ever executes a task). maintenance-run-service.ts is `run-due`/`cancel`'s sole orchestration point: reuses the existing M25 workspace-operation.lock (no new lock/transaction subsystem, per the build spec's WU45-02 stop condition) for the short read-select-claim sequence only; a handler exception or a stale (>5min, since every M45 task completes synchronously in-process) claim is always reconciled to a `failed` result, never left stuck or assumed successful. maintenance-task-handlers.ts is the typed dispatch registry: structural_review/defect_discovery call structuralReviewEngine/defectRemediationQueue's existing functions verbatim (runStructuralReview, discoverFromCheckpoints+applyDiscoveryCandidates) -- read-only structural review, discovery that never authorizes remediation. defect_remediation (WU45-04) selects at most one `queued` defect via defect-triage.ts's sortByQueuePriority, checks the schedule's own policy.maxAutomaticRisk ceiling (schema-bounded <=49) BEFORE calling prepareRemediation -- the exact function `aiqt defects remediate` calls, with no `approvedBy` (unattended) -- so a schedule can narrow the automation window but prepareRemediation's own internal >=50 human-approval gate remains the unconditional backstop either way. Deliberately stops short of bridging to live M36-M39 sandboxed execution (a materially new integration surface the build spec's WU45-04 stop condition reserved) -- the resulting RemediationDecision never carries an executionRef; validation must still be recorded separately via the existing `aiqt defects record-validation`.

structuralReviewContract.contractSummary: M43's StructuralFinding/StructuralReview/StructuralReviewDomain contract -- transient evidence objects, NOT part of canonical StateModel, never persisted to state.json or the runlog by review execution. findingKey excludes reviewCommit (stable across commits for the same real condition); reviewCommit is the separate Section-3.4 freshness binding. Significance/confidence are deliberately distinct types from M42's DefectSeverity/DefectConfidence.

structuralReviewEngine.contractSummary: `aiqt review structural [--domain]` / `aiqt review structural explain <findingKey>` -- read-only, offline-capable, bounded to 7 deterministic domain rule sets (ownership divergence, dependency cycles, responsibility hotspots, dead structural paths, public-contract drift, test-infrastructure hotspots reusing M35's classifyAllTestFiles, execution-safety-boundary duplication). Never mutates canonical state or appends a runlog event; nested under the existing `reviewCommand`, `aiqt review --mode` semantics unchanged. Full engineering history: docs/milestones/completed/m43/build-spec.md and closure-report.md.

structuralFindingDefectIntake.contractSummary: `aiqt defects intake-structural <findingKey>` -- the sole explicit, freshness-bound path from an M43 StructuralFinding into the M42 defect lifecycle (sourceKind "review_finding"). Verifies freshness (reviewCommit == current HEAD) and intake eligibility before reusing M42's applyDiscoveryCandidates verbatim -- no parallel defect pipeline. Intake only ever produces a `candidate`-status defect; it never triages, queues, or authorizes remediation. graphify-provider.ts is the only StructuralEvidenceProvider implementer: honestly reports unavailable (no Graphify integration exists), proving optional-provider isolation without fabricating one.
